mainTopic: Blank space between the text of a שטר and the signatures, and filling that gap with relatives' signatures
overview: The גמרא asks about a blank gap of a line and a half between the text of a שטר and the עדים' signatures. It first tries to answer from a ברייתא, but the beginning and end of that ברייתא point in opposite directions, so it proves nothing. A different ברייתא settles it: only a full two-line gap makes the שטר פסול, and anything less is כשר. That ברייתא also teaches that if one of four or five signers turns out to be a קרוב or otherwise פסול, the שטר still stands through the other witnesses. The גמרא says this supports חזקיה, who rules that a gap filled in with relatives' signatures is כשר. חזקיה compares this to a סוכה: empty space in the roof disqualifies at three טפחים, but סכך פסול disqualifies only at four. The amud ends by opening a new question about how the two-line gap is measured, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about a gap of a line and a half?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a blank gap of a line and a half between the text and the signatures makes a שטר פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים asked: if there is a gap of a line and a half, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question: is a gap of a line and a half between the document's text and the witnesses' signatures allowed? Step 4 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was already known that a two-line gap is a problem and a one-line gap is fine. The question is about the in-between case. Is one and a half lines treated like two (פסול) or like one (כשר)?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an unsolved question)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A line and a half, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means a blank gap of a line and a half between the text and the witnesses' signatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the in-between size of gap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a gap of one and a half lines between the text and the signatures makes the שטר פסול or leaves it כשר.

steps.title: Trying to prove it from the opening clause of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a two-line gap is פסול, which seems to suggest that a line and a half is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he placed the witnesses two lines away, the document is invalid. This implies that a line and a half is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by reading between the lines of a ברייתא that says a two-line gap is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names two lines as the problem. If two full lines are needed to make it פסול, then a line and a half, which is less than two, should be כשר. This is a proof by implication (a דיוק), not from an open statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (an attempt to prove something from a source)
But this... (introduces an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הִרְחִיק אֶת הָעֵדִים שְׁנֵי שִׁיטִין – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he distanced the witnesses two lines, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf. It means the signatures were placed two blank lines below the text.

phrases.english: But a line and a half is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הִרְחִיק אֶת הָעֵדִים שְׁנֵי שִׁיטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proposed answer to the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a line-and-a-half gap is כשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the ברייתא: only a two-line gap is פסול, implying anything less is כשר.

steps.title: The end of the same ברייתא implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The last clause says one line is כשר, which suggests a line and a half is פסול, so the ברייתא proves nothing either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last clause: one line is valid. Only one line is valid, which implies a line and a half is invalid! Rather, nothing can be learned from this ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by showing that the end of the same ברייתא points the other way. So it drops this ברייתא as a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning says 'two lines is פסול' (so maybe 1.5 is כשר). The end says 'one line is כשר' (so maybe 1.5 is פסול). The two implications contradict each other, so the ברייתא simply never addressed the in-between case.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last clause (look at the end of the source)
Nothing can be learned from it

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not contradicting itself. It just covered two clear cases (two lines, one line) and left the line-and-a-half case open. That is why no inference works.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
One line is valid.
It is only one line that is valid,
but a line and a half is invalid!
Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using this ברייתא at all to settle the line-and-a-half question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference from the רישא is cancelled out by the opposite inference from the סיפא.

steps.title: A different ברייתא settles it: less than two lines is כשר
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says outright that anything less than two lines is כשר, so a line and a half is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about it? Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: if he placed the witnesses two lines away from the text, it is invalid. Less than that is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final ruling is and brings a different ברייתא that answers the question directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first ברייתא, this one says openly 'פחות מכאן כשר', anything less than two lines is fine. Since a line and a half is less than two lines, it is כשר. This ends the question from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? (What is the final ruling?)
As it is taught in a ברייתא
The written text of the document

steps.whatToRemember: A blank gap of a full two lines between the text and the signatures makes a שטר פסול. Any smaller gap, including a line and a half, leaves it כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical measurement for a valid שטר. A gap of two lines is the point where someone could add forged text above the signatures.

phrases.english: What came of it?
Come and hear, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הִרְחִיק אֶת הָעֵדִים שְׁנֵי שִׁיטִין מִן הַכְּתָב – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he distanced the witnesses two lines from the text, it is invalid.
Less than this, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejected the first source, this brings a new source that answers step 1 directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gap of less than two lines, including a line and a half, is כשר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a full two-line gap makes the שטר פסול.

steps.title: One unfit witness among several does not ruin the שטר
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: if one of four or five signers is a relative or otherwise unfit, the testimony stands through the remaining witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If four or five witnesses signed the document and one of them turned out to be a relative or otherwise unfit, the testimony stands through the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a new rule: what happens when one signer on a שטר turns out not to be a valid witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because there are still at least two valid witnesses left, the שטר stays valid. The one unfit signer is simply ignored. He does not cancel out the testimony of the others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that on a שטר, one bad signature among several good ones does not disqualify the whole document.

phrases.english: If there were four or five witnesses
signed on the document,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל –
phrases.english: and one of them was found to be a relative or unfit,
the testimony shall stand through the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה עֵדִים חֲתוּמִין עַל הַשְּׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא from step 4, but on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one of several signing witnesses is a קרוב or פסול, the שטר is upheld through the remaining valid witnesses.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports חזקיה: a gap filled with relatives is valid
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that a document survives an unfit signer supports חזקיה, who says that if the gap is filled with relatives' signatures, the שטר is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports חזקיה, because חזקיה said: if someone filled the gap with relatives' signatures, the document is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא just quoted backs up a ruling of חזקיה. חזקיה says that a blank gap filled in with signatures of קרובים does not ruin the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if one of several signers is a קרוב, the שטר still stands through the others. That קרוב's signature may sit right under the text, between the text and the valid witnesses, and the שטר is still כשר. So a space taken up by relatives' signatures is not treated as a blank gap, which is exactly חזקיה's point.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him, a source that backs up someone's ruling
An early אמורא whose ruling is being supported
He filled it, meaning he filled the blank gap
Relatives, who are not allowed to serve as witnesses

phrases.english: This supports חזקיה,
as חזקיה said:
If he filled it with relatives, it is valid.
phrases.notes: "It" is the blank gap between the text and the real witnesses' signatures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further conclusion from the ברייתא in step 5: unfit signers do not cancel the document, so relatives can fill the gap.
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's ruling that a gap filled with relatives' signatures is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא (step 5) that the testimony stands through the remaining valid witnesses even if one signer is a relative or unfit

steps.title: Do not be surprised: the comparison to a סוכה roof
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה compares his ruling to סוכה: empty space disqualifies at three טפחים, but פסול סכך only at four, so filling a gap with פסול material can help.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not be surprised, because empty space in a סוכה's roof disqualifies it at three handbreadths, while unfit roofing material disqualifies it only at four.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה explains why his ruling makes sense by pointing to a similar rule in הלכות סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a סוכה, a three-טפח empty gap ruins the roof, but the same gap filled with סכך פסול is fine, since פסול material only ruins at four. Something unfit can still be better than nothing. In the same way, relatives' signatures are not valid testimony, but they still fill the empty gap so the שטר stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty air, an open gap in the סכך
Material not allowed to be used as סוכה roofing

steps.whyThisMatters: The comparison teaches a general idea: an unfit filler can still solve the problem of empty space, even though it does not count as the real thing.

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for empty space in a sukka disqualifies at three,
phrases.notes: The numbers here are measured in טפחים, handbreadths.

phrases.english: while unfit roofing disqualifies only at four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues חזקיה's statement, giving a parallel case to show his ruling is reasonable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Just as a three-טפח gap in a סוכה is fixed by filling it with פסול סכך, a gap in a שטר is fixed by filling it with relatives' signatures.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה: relatives' signatures can fill the dangerous gap in a שטר, just as פסול סכך can fill a gap in a סוכה roof.

steps.title: A new question about the two-line gap begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question about the two-line gap that the חכמים said makes a שטר פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: about the two lines that the חכמים spoke of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question about the two-line gap. The question itself is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2-4 settled that a gap of two lines is פסול. Now the גמרא wants to clarify something about how that two-line measure works. Only the opening words appear here, so the details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them, an open question the גמרא wants to settle

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
the two lines that they spoke of —
phrases.notes: This points back to the two-line gap from the ברייתא in step 2. The question continues right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of filling the gap and starts a new question about the exact two-line measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two-line gap that makes a שטר פסול is defined (the question is completed in the next part of the text).
